title: 25. Zero-Trust Identity & External Secrets
summary: Implement zero-trust workload attestation using SPIFFE/SPIRE, kernel-isolated sandboxed runtimes (gVisor/Kata), and centralized secret synchronization with External Secrets Operator (ESO).
learningObjectives: Attest workload identity cryptographically using SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Documents (SVID)
Isolate untrusted multi-tenant pods with gVisor runsc and Kata Containers using RuntimeClass
Synchronize sensitive database credentials from HashiCorp Vault into Kubernetes using SecretStore and ExternalSecret
Eliminate plaintext secret storage in Git repositories and developer workstations

curriculumModules.title: SPIFFE/SPIRE & Sandboxed Runtimes (gVisor / Kata)
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Zero-trust eliminates network-perimeter trust. SPIFFE assigns universal cryptographic identities (spiffe://domain/ns/sa) to workloads. Sandboxed runtimes (gVisor runsc) intercept syscalls in userspace to prevent kernel exploitation.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Multi-tenant financial workloads running under RuntimeClass: gvisor with SPIRE agent SVID attestation for microsegmentation.

curriculumModules.title: External Secrets Operator (ESO) & HashiCorp Vault KMS
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Storing secrets in Git (even sealed or encrypted) introduces key rotation overhead. ESO continuously synchronizes secrets from enterprise KMS (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager) into native Kubernetes Secrets.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: ClusterSecretStore connected to central Vault with automated 1-hour secret rotation and audit logging.

labs.title: Workload Attestation with SPIFFE/SPIRE & gVisor RuntimeClass
labs.scenario: A high-risk third-party payment parser must be deployed. Isolate it inside a gVisor sandboxed kernel environment and attest its identity using SPIFFE/SPIRE annotations.
labs.productionContext: Untrusted or user-supplied code should never execute directly against the host Linux kernel; gVisor virtualizes system calls in userspace.
objectives: Deploy the RuntimeClass gvisor with handler runsc
Deploy the payment-parser Pod using runtimeClassName: gvisor
Verify the SPIFFE identity spiffe.io/spire-managed annotation
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: gvisor
handler: runsc
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: payment-parser
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    spiffe.io/spire-managed: "true"
    spiffe.io/spiffe-id: "spiffe://kubelabs.internal/ns/production/sa/payment-sa"
  labels:
    app: payment-parser
spec:
  runtimeClassName: gvisor
  containers:
    - name: parser
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do sleep 30; done"]
      securityContext:
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

steps.title: Review RuntimeClass and Pod Definitions
steps.instruction: Open the Manifest Editor to examine the gvisor RuntimeClass and payment-parser Pod.

steps.title: Deploy Sandboxed Pod
steps.instruction: Apply the manifest to the production namespace.

steps.title: Verify RuntimeClass Assignment
steps.instruction: Confirm that payment-parser runs under the gvisor RuntimeClass.
steps.commandHint: kubectl get pod payment-parser -n production -o jsonpath={.spec.runtimeClassName}

validationRules.description: RuntimeClass gvisor exists with handler runsc
validationRules.name: gvisor
validationRules.remediation: Deploy RuntimeClass gvisor with handler: runsc.

validationRules.name: payment-parser
validationRules.remediation: Ensure spec.runtimeClassName is set to 'gvisor' on payment-parser.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Confirm that the RuntimeClass name matches 'gvisor' and handler is 'runsc'.

labs.title: External Secrets Operator (ESO) Synchronization with Vault
labs.scenario: Configure the External Secrets Operator to securely pull database credentials from HashiCorp Vault into a native Kubernetes Secret without exposing credentials in Git.
labs.productionContext: ESO decouples Kubernetes applications from specific cloud KMS vendors while keeping secrets rotated and synchronized in real time.
objectives: Deploy a SecretStore named vault-backend connected to HashiCorp Vault
Deploy an ExternalSecret named db-credential-sync targeting db-credentials
Verify secret creation and synchronization status
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: SecretStore
metadata:
  name: vault-backend
  namespace: production
spec:
  provider:
    vault:
      server: "https://vault.internal:8200"
      path: "secret"
      version: "v2"
---
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: db-credential-sync
  namespace: production
spec:
  refreshInterval: "1h"
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-backend
    kind: SecretStore
  target:
    name: db-credentials
    creationPolicy: Owner
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-credentials
  namespace: production
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: external-secrets
type: Opaque
data:
  username: "Y2xvdWRfYWRtaW4="
  password: "c3VwZXJzZWNyZXRwYXNz"

steps.instruction: Deploy the SecretStore, ExternalSecret, and synced Secret.

steps.instruction: Check that db-credentials exists in the production namespace.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary security benefit of using gVisor (runsc) as a Kubernetes RuntimeClass?
options: It provides a user-space kernel (Sentry) that intercepts and filters container system calls, preventing host kernel exploits
It speeds up CPU clock frequencies
assessmentQuestions.explanation: gVisor acts as an application kernel running in userspace, shielding the host Linux kernel from untrusted container code.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does External Secrets Operator (ESO) prevent secret leakage in GitOps workflows?
options: By eliminating raw secrets from Git; developers commit only declarative ExternalSecret references that fetch secrets dynamically from Vault/KMS at runtime
By deleting Git history on push
By requiring every developer to manually enter passwords on Slack
By converting all passwords into MD5 hashes
assessmentQuestions.explanation: With ESO, only non-sensitive ExternalSecret CRDs are stored in Git; the operator synchronizes actual secret values directly from KMS.
